# Isaiah Chapter 55 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 156r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/ISA_055_page_001.jpg

---

**55:1** "Ho [hoi], everyone [kol] who-thirsts [tsame], come [lekhu] to-the-waters [la-mayim]; and-whoever-has no [ein lo] money [kesef], come, buy [shivru] and-eat [ve'ikhelu]; and-come, buy without [be-lo] money and-without [u-ve-lo] price [mechir] wine [yayin] and-milk [ve-chalav]."

**55:6** "Seek [dirshu] YHWH while-he-may-be-found [be-himmatse'o]; call-upon-him [qere'uhu] while-he-is near [be-heyoto qarov]."

**55:8** "For my-thoughts [machshevotai] [are] not your-thoughts [machshevoteikhem], and-your-ways [darkeikhem] [are] not my-ways [derakhay]," declares YHWH.

**55:9** "For [as] the-heavens [shamayim] are-higher [gavhu] than-the-earth [me-ha-arets], so [ken] are-higher my-ways than-your-ways, and-my-thoughts than-your-thoughts."

**55:10** "For as the-rain [ha-geshem] comes-down [yered] and-the-snow [veha-sheleg] from-the-heavens and-there [shammah] does-not return [lo yashuv] — but [ki im] waters [hirvah] the-earth [ha-arets] and-causes-it-to-give-birth [veholidah] and-causes-it-to-sprout [vehitsmichah], and-gives [venatan] seed [zera] to-the-sower [la-zorea] and-bread [lechem] to-the-eater [la-okhel] —

**55:11** so will-be [yihyeh] my-word [devari] which goes-out [yetse] from-my-mouth [mi-pi]: it-will-not return [lo yashuv] to-me empty [reiqam], but [ki im] it-will-accomplish [asah] what I-desire [chafatsti], and-will-prosper [vehitsliach] [in the thing] for-which [asher] I-sent-it [shelachtiv]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "Come, everyone who thirsts":** The great invitation — the theological conclusion of Second Isaiah. Salvation is free, available to all, and described in the most basic human terms: water, bread, wine, milk. No prerequisites except thirst.

**v.10-11 — "as the rain comes down":** The word-of-God theology stated most clearly. God's word is an active agent — it goes out, accomplishes its purpose, and does not return empty. Like rain that waters and produces growth, the word produces what it describes.

*— EMET*
